'not-applicable' = no mathematics section; 'adjacent' = the shelf serves it as tools or the scope mirrors a researched sibling. The completeness check re-runs on every pass. exams.csSection: GATE CS paper (Computer Science and Information Technology), 10 sections
csUnits: S1 Engineering Mathematics: discrete mathematics (logic, sets, relations, functions, partial orders, lattices, monoids, groups, graphs, combinatorics), linear algebra, calculus, probability and statistics
S2 Digital Logic: Boolean algebra, combinational and sequential circuits, minimization, number representations and computer arithmetic (fixed and floating point)

S3 Computer Organization and Architecture: machine instructions and addressing modes, ALU data-path and control unit, instruction pipelining and hazards, memory hierarchy, I/O interface (interrupt and DMA)
S4 Programming and Data Structures: programming in C, recursion, arrays, stacks, queues, linked lists, trees, BSTs, binary heaps, graphs
S5 Algorithms: searching, sorting, hashing, asymptotic complexity, greedy, dynamic programming, divide-and-conquer, graph traversals, MST, shortest paths
S6 Theory of Computation: regular expressions and finite automata, CFGs and PDAs, pumping lemma, Turing machines, undecidability
S7 Compiler Design: lexical analysis, parsing, syntax-directed translation, runtime environments, intermediate code generation, local optimisation, data-flow analyses
S8 Operating System: system calls, processes, threads, IPC, concurrency and synchronization, deadlock, CPU and I/O scheduling, memory management and virtual memory, file systems
S9 Databases: ER model, relational algebra, tuple calculus, SQL, integrity constraints, normal forms, file organization and indexing (B/B+ trees), transactions and concurrency control
S10 Computer Networks: OSI and TCP/IP stacks, switching, data link layer, routing protocols, IP addressing and CIDR, ARP/DHCP/ICMP/NAT, UDP/TCP/sockets, DNS/SMTP/HTTP/FTP

exams.csSection: Paper 2: Computer Science and Applications (code 87), 10 units
csUnits: U1 Discrete Structures and Optimization: mathematical logic, sets and relations, counting and discrete probability, group theory, graph theory, Boolean algebra, linear programming, simplex, transportation and assignment, PERT-CPM

U2 Computer System Architecture: digital logic circuits and components, data representation, register transfer and microoperations, basic computer organization, machine/assembly programming, microprogrammed control, CPU, pipeline and vector processing, I/O organization, memory hierarchy, multiprocessors

U3 Programming Languages and Computer Graphics: language design and translation, elementary data types, programming in C, OOP, programming in C++, web programming (HTML, XML, servlets), computer graphics (raster algorithms, 2D and 3D transforms, viewing, curves, surfaces, rendering)
U4 DBMS: database concepts and architecture, data modeling, SQL, normalization, enhanced data models, data warehousing and data mining, big data (MapReduce, Hadoop, HDFS), NoSQL

U5 System Software and Operating System: compilers, interpreters, loaders, linkers, macros, process management, threads, CPU scheduling, deadlocks, memory management, storage, file and I/O systems, security, virtual machines, Linux, Windows, distributed systems
U6 Software Engineering: process models (prescriptive and agile), requirements, design, quality (McCall, ISO 9126), estimation (COCOMO), testing, configuration management

U7 Data Structures and Algorithms: the structure census, performance analysis, design techniques, lower bound theory, graph algorithms, complexity theory (P/NP), number-theoretic/FFT/string algorithms, parallel and approximation algorithms

U8 Theory of Computation and Compilers: formal languages, regular languages and automata, CFLs and PDAs, Turing machines, unsolvable problems, syntax/semantic analysis, run-time system, intermediate code, code generation and optimization

U9 Data Communication and Computer Networks: data communication, network models and OSI/TCP-IP layers, IPv4/IPv6, WWW (DNS, SMTP, FTP), network security (cryptography, steganography, VPN, firewalls), mobile technology (GSM, CDMA), cloud computing and IoT

U10 Artificial Intelligence: approaches to AI (Turing test, rational agents, heuristic search, game playing, minimax, alpha-beta), knowledge representation, planning, NLP, multi-agent systems, fuzzy sets, genetic algorithms, artificial neural networks
